tasks.title: Deploy gates: supply the production hostname, then verify offline
tasks.goal: Deploy gates: supply the production hostname, then verify offline
tasks.description: BOTH GATES CLOSED 2026-10-13. The production hostname was never missing: the Worker is live at https://comp3tive.dimasawardhana.workers.dev/, and wrangler.jsonc's name "comp3tive" is the REAL Worker name (a workers.dev host is <worker>.<account>.workers.dev), not the documented placeholder four documents called it. It serves master at 3683974 BYTE-IDENTICALLY -- index.html, app/index.html, 404.html, sw.js, manifest.webmanifest and all 17 precached assets diffed clean against a worktree build of that commit. Gate 2: the deployed host sends NO Vary header anywhere (checked /, /app/, /sw.js, /manifest.webmanifest, /404.html, a hashed asset, a font, an icon; HEAD and GET with/without Accept-Encoding), so cache.match has nothing to honour and { ignoreVary: true } is HARMLESS rather than load-bearing -- the branch's "largest unverified assumption" is retired. Gate 3: e2e/live/offline.spec.ts (npm run e2e:live) drives Cloudflare's edge with a real Chromium and passes 4 tests across 3 consecutive runs -- no request leaves the origin; a whole round-robin tournament (15 players -> 3 teams -> 3 BO3 fixtures -> champion) runs with the network cut on the deployed build, holding exactly ["comp3tive-b12c14230adf"] and 23 precached entries; the deployed VERSION b12c14230adf RECOMPUTES from the live origin's own 23 responses (so the hash sees content, not a typed string); and a planted stale comp3tive- cache is purged on the genuine first activation while a foreign some-other-app-cache is left alone. Corrections shipped in README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/adr/0007, docs/adr/0008, .scratch/backend/spec.md, .scratch/backend/issues/04, .scratch/landing-page/issues/05, wrangler.jsonc. Residual for Phase E (not a gate): a CUSTOM DOMAIN, because a *.workers.dev host is on the Public Suffix List's private section and can never share a passkey with a custom domain. Method note: the first draft of the purge test re-registered an unchanged worker and asserted a purge that could not have fired (browsers byte-compare the script and skip activate); it failed, and the fix -- plant caches before the real first install -- is recorded in the spec. Verified: tsc -b exit 0, 788 unit tests pass, 117/117 local e2e pass, npm run build clean.

Ticket 01's export call site (App.tsx:416) is now src/shell/useAppCommands.ts:199; ticket 01's merge loop (App.tsx:435-474) and ticket 02's JSON id rule (App.tsx:572) are src/shell/usePlayerImport.ts:282-294 and :350; ticket 05's swallowed catch (App.tsx:308-313) is src/shell/useSplitFlow.ts:257 and its orphan-repair effect is src/shell/useLegacyAdoption.ts; ticket 06's tb- try/catch (App.tsx:93-108) is src/shell/usePreferences.ts. tasks.title: Cover the roster editor's refusal with a test
tasks.goal: Cover the roster editor's refusal with a test
tasks.description: CLOSED 2026-10-13. The roster editor's refusal (PlayerEditModal.tsx:141-146 -- validates, sets .field-errors, returns before onSave) now has a test, and it had to be a BROWSER case: e2e/tests/roster/editor-refusal.spec.ts. The prediction in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN's known-open row ('one unit case') was wrong and the spec says why -- PlayerEditModal.test.ts renders via renderToStaticMarkup, which runs no event handlers, so save() is unreachable from that layer; and the repo has no jsdom, no testing library and no *.test.tsx (vite.config.ts test.include is only src/**/*.test.ts), with README stating the convention outright. validatePlayer's own rules were already unit-tested; what was untested was the WIRING, and wiring needs a click. THE SPEC: two cases -- the refusal (modal stays open, .field-errors carries the validator's own sentence, the player is not on the roster after closing) and a control (same dialog, same session, saves fine with no capability). MUTATION-VERIFIED: deleting the early return in PlayerEditModal.save turns the refusal case RED while the control stays green, so it pins the refusal and not the dialog; PlayerEditModal.tsx was restored byte-identical (git diff empty). FINDING WHILE WRITING IT, recorded not fixed: five of the six refusal rules are UNREACHABLE from the shipped UI -- ratings always carry a value, DisciplineEditModal hardcodes {min:1,max:5} with no bounds input so no scale wide/fractional enough to render a free number field can exist, buildCapabilities heals a stray preferred role AND an emptied eligibility list by falling back to all roles, and duplicates are filtered out of the add-a-capability strip. The one reachable path is a discipline that declares NO ROLES: DisciplineEditModal permits saving one (untick 'Roles are required'), and validateCapability then demands an eligible role from an empty list -- the dialog refuses with NO CONTROL THAT CAN CLEAR IT, since the eligible-roles strip maps the discipline's own empty role list. Refusing the discipline at creation vs relaxing the player rule are both product decisions, so the spec's header records the dead end rather than closing it. RECORDS: app-correctness/03's open coverage row closed with the mutation evidence and the unreachability analysis; IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN's known-open row struck through. ALSO FIXED: my new spec made README's 'The 32 specs' stale -- a claim TASK-106 had JUST installed a rule about -- so the count is REMOVED rather than updated to 33, since it has now gone stale three times (22 -> 32 -> 33); ROADMAP records the third staleness. Verified: tsc -b exit 0, 788/788 unit, 119/119 browser (117 existing + 2 new), build clean.
